[b]An Nabai News[/b]

[i]26 October 2026 | 15 Jumada 1448 AH[/i]

[u]Doves, Opposition Concerned About Baladullahan Shift to Military Operations Against Non-State Actors[/u]

With Baladullahan troops and drones now involved in fighting against both the GB terrorist organization and the ISV, the more peace supporting members of the Grand Majlisi, as well as peace activists and some opposition figures, are speaking out and protesting against what they say is a possible slippery slope into the government legalizing offensive actions as pre emptive strikes against not just non-state actors, but states as well.

Since the Constitution of 1992, it had been considered inappropriate for the government to get involved with military operations of any kind unless they were strictly defensive and to protect our citizens here or abroad explained Melak Hamazi, professor of International Relations and Law at al-Ilm University in Baghlata. But the change of that doctrine last year, and the country getting into military alliances and sending troops across the world is a radical departure from the core foreign policy principles of this nation. Yes, of course the government says this is only to fight against non-state actors in defense of our allies. But if decades of established precedent can be changed overnight, it isnt impossible that this doctrine will go further, to operations against other nations. In shaa Allah this does not happen, but it has to be pointed out. 

Theres nothing in Baladullahan law that explicitly states we cant enter into defensive pacts or form military alliances with other nations, and I find that argument absurd, to say the least commented Ishaq al-Maliki, chairman of the NGO Lawyers for Justice and former Senior Legal Advisor to President Marwan al-Haq (1999-2004). The norms that emerged from the Neutrality Clause in the 1992 Constitution were political decisions, not something written in stone. The Neutrality Clause itself stated Baladullah will not wage aggressive war of any kind against a state actor or a non-state actor not classified as a terrorist organization, and will restrict its scope of military activities to defensive actions to defend the territorial integrity, sovereignty, and people of Baladullah here or abroad OR to defend an allied nation from aggression by a terrorist non-state entity. 

Either way, this clause was altered even as early as the Constitution of 2009 to open up the possibility of defensive war on behalf of an ally against state and non state actors. We have always been a peace loving country, of course, but the last year has seen unprecedented dangers against our allies and ourselves from extremist organizations.

Around 10,000 people marched in Medinah al-Islam against sending more troops to fight non state actors, and around 50,000 in Maghlaba. Counter protests of around 20,000 in Medinah al Islam and 5,000 in Maghlaba were also reported, with no violence recorded.

[u]National Electoral Council Finds No Evidence of Fraud or Deliberate Misconduct During May Elections; 75,000 Protest in Maghlaba[/u]

The final report of the NEC investigation into the irregularities and glitches during the May elections concluded that despite some technological errors and miscounted votes during the day of the elections, recounts and system updates rectified any voting issues that took place. No deliberate acts of voter fraud or tampering were found to have taken place. While most people, even opposition supporters, accepted this verdict, in some cities like Maghlaba, this lead to angry protests.

During the protests in Maghlaba on 24 October, riots and attacks on police took place, while 3 police stations were torched in the city. 500 people were arrested and 150 wounded (including 70 police officers) by the end of the day. Smaller protest encampments are still ongoing, and a movement calling itself Citizens for Real Change has emerged. [/spoiler]

Upon the dawn of the 18th Drømm would call a special session of the legislature announcing that the old constitution would be dissolved and the powers of the government would be transferred to the Principates. 

Following this he would suspend the gøsfodde, sending the representatives home to their districts, to Face their constitutents. 

As the evening came he would convene a special meeting with the five princes quietly drafting an agreement of principles, those being decentralization, freedom, and stability. He would order the princes to hold constitutional conventions in their respective principates and send representatives to the capital to form a new government.

[spoiler=[b]The Revolution is Everywhere[/b]][b]The Revolution is Everywhere[/b]

Communism has seemingly erupted everywhere. In Astanir, QASIC forces have triumphed over all other enemy actors and established in Astan a people's republic. Sanguivallis's cities are now the sacred pilgrimages for any seeking to attune to the monumental works of modern socialism. Qianxun is seemingly on track to break out of middle power status through its aggressive geopolitical strategy of exporting the revolution everywhere. Gythena is in freefall, waiting for a red banner to catch it.

People fear change, and when people fear, they often choose a scapegoat upon which to blame all uncertainties. In this case, the people of the West might blame MZP general secretary Cui Fangf, or perhaps Argo Lo Pilato, the theoretician of the Socialist International, or else Horano Benir, who is responsible for granting the Socialist International a mandate to intercede on behalf of collapsing nation states. These individuals have all indeed been instrumental in safeguarding the revolution in their respective nation states, though their actions have largely occurred as reactions, collaborations, fabrications out of necessity, bereft of any particular inclination towards a wider goal.

Communism is on the rise, but its great and final progenitor is someone who has, thus far, escaped the scrutiny of the world. Someone who, in all honesty, has no business fraternizing with the red banner at all.

It was October, at a certain quiet coffeehouse called "Tage's", on the corner of Ipsen and 5th Street, Stormhaven. On the outside, Tage's was a simple establishment, with a dainty wooden exterior and a simple sign on which was inscribed the special drink of the day in humble chalk. It was the kind of shop students would flock to for their Sunday dates. The seats were mahogany with green cushioning, color-coded to emulate the design of the shop signage, and to the analytical eye, these seats counted together accumulated to maybe around 19 individuals at greatest capacity.

However, ask the barista for a certain drink laced with orange syrup (that tastes rancid, mind, to prevent it being ordered by accident) and she will guide you into the storage rooms where a trap door allows access deeper into Tage's.

At first, you are greeted by dull concrete, as if to disguise to any accidental adventurers that, in this door, is merely an emergency exit or banal storage area. Walk deeper, and you are greeted by a grand room, roughly double the size of the aboveground. The mahogany returns, and the green cushioning, and the chalked-written sign too, but it no longer talks about the daily special. Instead, on it was the agenda of the day:

[list]

[i][pre]ON RECENT EVENTS[/PRE][/i]

[/list]

"You lead revolutions well, Mr. Almstedt." Cui Fang said, patting Xavier on the back before settling down in his seat. In his hand was a simple glass of water, for he had little tolerance for caffeine. His tone was jovial, and for good reason, too. "Have you not considered taking the next step of registering yourself in your own communist party? If you want, the Min Zhu Party can provide you with all the funding you need."

"Haha, no worries about that, general secretary," Xavier replied, shrugging off Cui with a chuckle. "Almstedt Corporation is here purely because we want to do things right by the common man. People need wages to thrive in a cut-throat world that doesn't give a single sh-t about them, and we provide that. I'm a very kind man, but kindness doesn't mean I have to be a commi-... ahem... a communist..."

"A fellow traveler is the first in a series of heroic duties at the end of which is the creation of the party cadre. You may think yourself a pragmatist for now, Comrade Almstedt, in that your corporations merely serve us for their own benefit, but soon you shall realize that these communist governments you've installed are what will awaken you to our mighty cause."

"Whatever you say, general secretary... Oh and look, the Sangs are here."'

Xavier pointed to the secret entrance. Descending from the concrete staircases were two individuals, both wearing the elaborate dress uniforms of the Sanguinian state. The man, Argo Lo Pilato, could hardly be mistaken thanks to his bright red hair that could never seem to be brushed down properly. Nor could the women be mistaken either, with her thick sunglasses and bright golden Chi-Rho symbol that proudly shone on her left chest.

[list]

"Comrade Almstedt, Comrade Cui." Argo greeted, speaking in a voice that bordered on whispering, as though acting in quiet deference to the conversation Xavier and Cui had been conducting earlier. "And this is Comrade Terrasi, she was with me during the Red Embassy to the Montfleurois Kingdom. The one with the steel shipments?"

"Somare, I know about you." Xavier quipped, adjusting his glasses as he took a deep look at Terrasi. "Immacolata Terrasi, right? You've been the talk of the industry recently, back in Stormhaven. People were wondering why Sanguinian supercars and television sets suddenly started appearing at CIO malls and Hypercenters all over Vespuria. Guess it's your fault."

"Guilty as charged!" Terrasi replied with a chuckle.

[/list]

"Alright, enough capitalist discussions, everyone." Cui Fang proclaimed, concluding their brief introductions. "Remember, you're only represented in this council because, as fellow travelers of the revolution, we consider you to be indispensable assets in challenging the liberal international order from within. Ultimately, the goal of any revolution is the transition to communism and the heralding of the classless society, no matter how long or difficult it may take, and that goes for your respective corporations as well. Do I make myself clear?"

"Of course, of course, general secretary." Xavier yawned, waving off the general secretary. "Anyways, what's this about?"

"It concerns recent events on Elseyr." Cui Fang answered, turning to Argo. "Comrade Lo Pilato, as I've understood, you sent a delegation to Gythena to gauge its propensity for revolution. How has that gone so far?"

"Er, yeah... Comrade Almstedt and I organized that joint mission a while ago..." Argo began, his face a flurry of confused emotions. It has been a tense few days in Gythena after all, and whatever mandate Socialist International had given the Sanguinians had evolved so far beyond what they had initially been intended to do. With a deep breath, Argo continued. "... Listen, Comrade Cui, it seems things have changed drastically since we sent that delegation to Gythena."

[list]

"How so?"

"Mr. Almstedt knows a bit more. I've just been receiving fragmentary intel from my point of contact, Comrade Sferrazza."

"What does Comrade Almstedt here have to do with this?"

[/list]

"... Oh crap!" Xavier suddenly jumped, at first shocked, then breaking out into a deep laugh. It was the kind of laugh you'd hear after a particularly cruel prank, or a realization of one's abject stupidity. The kind that grates on the ears like cutlery scraping against a plate. "Ahahaha! Right, so it's THAT mess... Sorry, sorry, ahem... so, uh, long story short, Mr. Lo Pilato here hired Almstedt Corporation to work security, it was something to do with budgeting, since they had to run a deficit to pay for that huge operation in Astanir..."

"You sent SummitONE?" Cui Fang inquired.

"Nah, MROS Dynamics."

"That's... no different?"

"Correct, but let's pretend they are for the sake of appearances," Xavier answered, grinning widely. "Well, so basically, the Sanguinians had to transition from diplomats to surprise revolutionaries. I have a good man in Gythena at the moment, a certain Ulf de Mayne. You should know him from the operations in Sal-Baliz. As we're speaking, he is currently fighting tooth and nail with a bunch of my boys in Häliskirk."

"The Gythenans accepted MROS Dynamics's aid?" Cui Fang reacted with surprise. After all, he did expend quite a bit of Qianxun's foreign aid budget into Pax International to shore up public support for Daijunist Socialism, and now it seemed that Xavier, a capitalist of the lowest order, was accomplishing the same tasks on a faster scale with barely a fraction of the funds.

"Something like that," Xavier said, easing the general secretary's concerns. "The fact of the matter is, honestly, that communism is now in vogue after all these months of constant tension and escalation between the powers of Elseyr and beyond. THEP is no longer the uncontested hegemony it once was; it's now being challenged by EDU with its gigantic military-industrial complexes. In private markets, we're taught that competition breeds innovation, but this recent competition between these two alliances has done the complete opposite to global markets. Entities with long exposure to arms manufacturing, such as myself, are happy with recent developments, of course, but everything else has been very, very speculative. Tourism? Food? Luxury goods? Textiles? Everything's been constantly between acceleration and breaking because the liberal democracies haven't been behaving. Who suffers when private markets are constantly beaten down by uncertainty?"

[list]

"The people!" Terrasi interrupted instinctively.

"The people!" Xavier exclaimed. "The people are getting f-cked over every step of the way because of war. As the cost of living rises, more people begin to suffer. More suffering! It is because of suffering that we are winning everywhere!"

[/list]

There was a sudden silence in the room. The participants of the secret meeting awkwardly exchanged glances, then turned back to Xavier, waiting for him to apologize for that strange remark. Instead, he doubled down. 

"Crises are good, ladies and gentlemen. As more people suffer, this grand design we've created for ourselves accelerates towards its critical mass. Now get a good look at Gythena and see what's been going on. It's a humble northern nation nestled into the heart of EDU territory, but it barely interacts with its neighbors. Its biggest trading partner is the Neue Republik, but trade volumes in recent months have started to dry up because of EDU's constant push and pull against THEP. And so, Gythena tries interacting with THEP through the Vespurians and Sanguinians, but then came the war in Tallisland. Ports are blockaded, ships need to go the long way, imports become pricier, and natural industry starts to lag behind. Mr. Cui, you seem to be curious as to why my boys have been making good progress capturing Gythena's capital city. Let me tell you now that it's because things are currently in our favor, and they will continue to be in our favor so long as the liberal international order continues to cannibalize itself from the inside out."

"... You said that the men have been making good progress in Häliskirk..." Cui Fang meekly interjected, hoping to steer the discussion away from Xavier's iron pragmatism. "Does this mean that the Socialist International has taken Gythena under its wing?"

"Rather than answer that myself, because quite frankly I have no idea, I should just phone a friend." Xavier coolly responded, suddenly standing up from the table and taking his phone out of his coat pocket.

...

...

...

Eventually, after a few seconds of standing on ceremony, someone picks up on the other side.

"Hello?" said a monotonous, female voice. It was the kind of voice you'd hear on an early morning call to a bank. "Let's see here... this number is... Mr. Almstedt?..."

"Yo Irja, you're on call with the Presidium." Xavier casually elaborated. "I'm putting you on speaker, introduce yourself, yeah? I'm showing off my dearest new associates in Gythena at the moment."

"... I see, very well," Irja replied, nonplussed by the sudden pedestal.

Xavier leaned further into the table and set the phone up in the center, opening the speakers, and maximized Irja's screen, prompting Fang, Argo, and Immacolata to shift their seats over to face the phone opposite. A few seconds later, Irja came into view. She was a pale-faced woman, of a complexion somewhere between Teutonic and the morgue, as was usually the case with the Gythenan people. Her hair was the same, a kind of blonde that blended into ingots of solid gold, and with light blue eyes that contrasted with the dull outcast of the sky above where Irja was standing.

"Greetings, everyone." She began, after taking a bit to focus her camera. "My name is Irja Evesti, though in the recent operations around Häliskirk I have been identified among the Red Guards as Toveri Otava. I am an associate professor for the University of Polijamsa's Department of Environmental Science and formerly chief editor for [i]Avain[/i]. As of right now, I am the Chair of the Congress of People's Deputies, a provisional body that the communes have provisionally installed to guide the Gythenan Commonwealth."

[list]

"Good day, Comrade Evesti. You are currently speaking to the Presidium of the Socialist International."

"I am aware," Irja replied, noting each of the four individuals who were pressed together, all eyes fixed on her like birds circling a helpless prey. "I am assuming that Mr. Almstedt called me to discuss events in Gythena?"

[/list]

"Something like that," Argo said, jumping into the discussion. "Comrade Evesti, I am Argo Lo Pilato. You may be familiar with me, since Ulf de Mayne probably identified me as his employer when MROS Dynamics freed you from the prison system. We called because we wanted to understand if Socialist International has succeeded in building ground for Gythena's transition to socialism, or if you are still in the preliminary stages and require intervention as had been done in Astanir."

"Ah... in that case, this call is unnecessary, Comrade Lo Pilato," Irja said matter-of-factly. "As of this very moment, the Red Guards have received the palatial Gythenan flag from the acting mayor of Häliskirk. As far as the world is concerned, the revolution is now the government of Gythena. Ulf de Mayne has done wonders for the cause, and now he has transitioned from leading an insurgency to leading a regular military force tasked with suppressing the last of the counterrevolution. The Kommunardit of Gythena are presently of the opinion that political strategy may now shift towards implementing the New Order while de Mayne's forces accomplish their mandate."

"... We'll make this quick then... I can't believe events have proceeded this quickly without my input..." Cui lamented, taking a moment to process Irja's rapid-fire information. "... Comrade Evesti, does your Gythenan government accede to the seven policies of the Socialist International? In the fight against decadent liberalism? And the dictatorship of the proletariat? Of a rejection of left and right deviations from the people's revolution? And of the protracted people's war?"

[list]

"To all things, we accede," Irja replied instantaneously. "In fact, Gythena may well be a practical model for the praxis that Socialist International believes any socialist state must follow."

"Very well," Cui says, contented. "Let us meet in Citharo when the world has calmed down, Comrade Evesti."

"And you too, general secretary. Comrade Lo Pilato, Terrasi, and Mr. Almstedt."

[/list]

The call then cut, and they are left with a black screen and their own bewildered faces. Xavier smirked as he watched the three members of the Presidium quietly discuss among themselves for a moment. It was as Xavier had told. The communist revolution was suddenly erupting everywhere, and it was not waiting for them to make ready.

"Comrade Almstedt, how confident are you that these events will also happen in Thyven and Vespuria?" Cui asked Xavier pointedly.

"About as confident as a daredevil stuffing himself into a cannon," Xavier answered, the grin on his face never dissipating. "If you ever wanted the power to will the spoken word into reality, general secretary, now is your chance..."

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Red Unionism[/b]]

[b]Red Unionism[/b]

Strange bulletins would seemingly begin to erupt overnight in Northern Vespurias, claiming to be authored by an organization called the "Communist League", which among other things demanded the restoration of the political union between Thyven and Vespurias, the adoption of the [i]summa potestas[/i] theory of government, the unification of the various Socialist Coalition Parties in Vespuria and socialist clubs in Thyven into a single communist party, and lastly integration into the Socialist International to combat the neo-fascism of the Elseyran Defense Union and the Free Nations Treaty Organization.

Below is one such bulletin, found nailed to a prominent bridge in Cedarwyck:

[list]

[i]As the White Tree crisis draws to a close, Vespuria could finally rest as a chaotic chapter in the storied history of its nation finally ends.

 Or so it seems! 

With the final calming of the White Tree, the Vespurian Commonwealth has unchained the demon whose name is decentralization. In the past, as the Commonwealth of High Albany, all political power was ensconced within the great city of Kingsmount. Then, on unification, Hyperion. When people turned to the Vespurian nation, they really turned to the core.

However, now all eyes are turned to the periphery, to Burrow, Stormhaven, to Cedarwyck and Wynskar! Here in the north is the progress towards a certain perfection unachieved by relentless years of thoughtless liberalism! As the tide of terror recedes and we mourn the fallen, the rights of the work sound louder than ever! O people of Erene, will ye not rise as your tyrants have risen?

To those present and come: A demonstration of the Communist League of Vespuria shall be scheduled on the 15th of October 2026. Those seeking to participate, please get in touch with Mr. Dag Sparre at 61 Cedarwyck in the United Guilds right extension to receive further information.

WORKERS OF THE WORLD, UNITE![/i]

[/list]

Since the end of the White Tree crisis, the Vespurian Empire had been infiltrated by several hundred sleeper agents from the Sanguinian Democratic Republic, operating under Xavier Almstedt's payroll, who had been tasked with spreading the cause of the Socialist International to the Northern States of Vespuria, which had contributed the most to the Separate Group of Forces. With generous funding thanks to Citharo, these agents had been steadfast in committing to three major goals:

[list]

1. Coordinating discussions with the various factions of the disjointed Socialist Coalition Party, principally in the hopes of unifying them into a "Communist League" that adheres solely to the principles of Dai Jun Thought.

2. Radicalizing the student youth who had been worst affected by the White Tree crisis, particularly those who lost family members, friends, acquaintances, who have good reason to blame the national government for their personal tragedies.

3. Orchestrating hostile takeovers of corporations operating at the state-level, pressuring boards of directors into adopting clauses on shareholder rights, then transferring corporate assets to Almstedt Corporation, which acts as an intermediary for these agents.

[/list]

At the moment, these efforts have gone by mostly unnoticed by the wider Vespurian public, but since the recent successes in Astanir and Gythena, both Almstedt Corporation and Socialist International have increased funding for their agents, leading to record numbers of new communist cadres just in Norrhollow alone, with the Radical and Moderate Parties of Norrhollow reporting massive drops in memberships as a result.

Through these endeavors, the Socialist International hopes to slowly but surely chip away at the traditional liberal blocs controlling Vespuria's government, but continued activities in the country are contingent upon the success of the Gythenan Revolution, which is by now completely guaranteed.

The great socialist design of the International had been set in place by a series of dominoes that had begun to fall long ago, first in Qianxun, then Sanguivallis, then Astanir, then Gythena, Vespurias. With fortitude and luck, the next domino piece may then land in Thyven, and through it all of THEP, perhaps all Erene. For now, as Citharo waits for the eruption of a great communist rising in Vespurias, MZP general secretary Cui Fang would authorize a fresh set of Sanguinian agents to travel to North Thyven too and assess the willingness of that state's leftist party to obey Citharo's political line.

[/spoiler]
